description: Known table of the current violations of the rule "a subpackage's public API is only effects and handlers" (read by tests/test_public_api_known_violations.py).
The key of a name is (package dir, module that exports the name, name) — the rows of the tools/public_api_inventory.py inventory whose kind is neither effect nor handler (other, unclassified).

A submodule that does not start with _ is a row whose module field is (submodule) and whose name is the import name of the submodule (ADR-DOE-API-001 R5 — packages in scope use the group "Violation — hide the submodule with _"; packages awaiting a scope answer use the group "Boundary — foundation/tool package"). Once it is hidden by prefixing the name with _, remove it from the table.

A name moved from a submodule to the entry point (the import root) is read as the same row without rewriting the table's module: if the submodule still exports the same name, only when the definition site is the same; if it no longer exports it, by name and root alone.

The table only shrinks: the names of the "names" groups are limited to names present in the version of the commit that added this file (the check compares with the first version in git history). Submodule rows are limited to those present in the version of the commit that added the submodule rows. Remove fixed names from the table (a name that is in the table but not in the inventory is red).
A name that has no choice but to be added is written in "added_names", one row each with package, module, name and reason.

The group names (split — direction of the fix, kind of boundary) were copied from the document that separated violations from boundaries (the split of the doeff 5b1accad6 inventory — a machine proposal). How scope and boundaries are treated awaits the answer to the question.

scope "awaiting scope answer" = foundation/tool packages (when the answer comes, the owner cuts a card and fixes scope and group). Today there are 0 packages — the last one, doeff-adr, was moved to "in scope" (ADR-DOE-API-001 R33).

Components inside doeff (packages/doeff-vm — the VM that only doeff's root package imports) are outside the inventory's scope and are not listed in the table (ADR-DOE-API-001 R11 — the 64 rows of scope "awaiting scope answer" and group "Boundary — foundation/tool package" were removed). The same test that reads the table also checks that files outside doeff do not import the component's import root.

The group "Violation — reshape as a handler-returning factory" became empty and disappeared. It held the names that the 2026-10-28 decision (ADR-DOE-API-001 R6) treats as handler-returning factories but whose current shape does not fit the factory structure. maybe, result, on_raise and absent_as had their old shapes removed and left the table. scheduled is not made a factory under the 2026-10-30 policy (a handler with neither settings nor per-call state is not a factory — ADR-DOE-API-001 R6, ADR-DOE-API-002 R1) but a handler value carrying the mark _doeff_is_handler_fn — the inventory reads it as a handler, so it left the table.

Names that the rule allowed name by name (group "Allowed — …") are not placed in this table; they are placed, with a basis (an ADR rule or one sentence giving the reason), in the allowed table tests/data/public_api_allowed.json — this table holds only violations and boundaries and may become empty (ADR-DOE-API-001 R12). The 280 rows of the group "Allowed — program helper" were moved there.

The 247 rows (16 packages, 129 names) of the group "Boundary — exception type" were moved to the allowed table with the basis ADR-DOE-API-001 R2, because the allowed group "Allowed — exception type", whose shape the inventory verifies (a child class of BaseException defined by that package), was added; the group disappeared.

The 757 rows (278 names) of the group "Boundary — effect value type" were moved because the allowed group "Allowed — effect value type", whose shape the inventory verifies (types that appear in the annotation of a field of an effect class exposed by the same package — the inventory's value_types), was added: the 95 names with 298 rows that fit the shape and the 25 rows of "added names" moved to the allowed table with the same answer as basis, and the group disappeared. Of the names that do not fit, the 25 names with 107 rows that appear in the effect answer type (__doeff_answer__) of the same package moved to the group "Boundary — effect result type", and the remaining 158 names with 352 rows moved to the group "Violation — annotate the effect field or move inside" — value types the effect field annotation does not state (object, bare tuple or dict, Any) and names that appear in no effect field. If it is an effect value type, write the type in the field annotation and move it to the allowed table; otherwise move it inside.

The 41 names of doeff-core-effects in the group "Violation — annotate the effect field or move inside" were sorted name by name: the 14 names with 39 rows that the inventory reads as effect answer types moved to the group "Allowed — effect answer type" of the allowed table; the 8 names with 14 rows of handler scripts, settings and factory-argument types (MeterBucket, RaiseCase, SchedulerImplementation, ScriptedUpstream, ScriptedWs*) moved to the group "Boundary — handler setting type"; the 6 handler-internal parts (SqlText, SqlPlaceholder, DriverValue, WsCloseFrame, VmWork, TraceSink — 0 callers in outside repos) were removed from the entry point and the old-path fixed lists and left the table. For the remaining 9 names (ComputeLoad, InterpreterFacts, ProcessInputWritten, ProcessNotChild, ProcessRunning, ModuleFound, WarmRunning, HttpPhases, HttpFailureKind), the effects now state their answer types, so their 25 rows moved to the group "Allowed — effect answer type" of the allowed table. PRIORITY_HIGH, PRIORITY_IDLE, PRIORITY_NORMAL and Resumption were settled as follows: the task priority became the IntEnum TaskPriority (IDLE, NORMAL, HIGH), written in the annotation of the priority field of Spawn, Wait and Race, and placed in the group "Allowed — effect value type" of the allowed table. The 3 old constants were removed from the entry point and the old path doeff_core_effects.scheduler after the 8 caller files in agora-controllers were rewritten to TaskPriority and doeff-min-commit was raised (agora-controllers 27188d6c), and this group of doeff-core-effects became empty and disappeared (the order of ADR-DOE-API-001 R20). Resumption is neither an effect field nor an answer but vocabulary for declaring effect types, so it is placed only inside (doeff_core_effects._effects — the place ADR-DOE-CORE-EFFECTS-003 R15 names), and doeff-hy and tests read it from there (0 callers in outside repos).

The group "Violation — write the effect's answer type" was separated from effect result types by the machine proposal; it holds names that no effect of the package writes as an answer type (the T of EffectBase[T] or :answer of defeffect) — the answers of effects that wrote the answer only in a docstring, and names that are no effect's answer. The fix is either to write the answer type in the answering effect and move it to the group "Allowed — effect answer type" of the allowed table, or to move names that no effect answers to an inner module (of the 1,034 rows of the group "Boundary — effect result type", the 603 rows that the inventory reads as answer types were moved to the allowed table and the remaining 431 rows to this group. Fix package by package).

The 62 rows of the group "Violation — annotate the effect field or move inside" of the small 14 packages were split: the 24 rows of effect answer and value types moved to the allowed table; the 10 rows of settings and argument types passed to handlers (among them Drop and WhenUnsent of doeff-events and NotificationCapture of doeff-notify) moved to the group "Boundary — handler setting type"; the 9 rows of names that the sibling cards writing type aliases of answers put in answers (NoticeSent and NoticeGapTold of doeff-events; SeedreamImage of doeff-seedream) moved to the group "Violation — write the effect's answer type"; and the 19 names with 19 rows that appear in no effect were moved inside and removed. The 3 rows of choice, noul and score of doeff-system-one have many callers in outside repos, so they stay and will be fixed in a separate change.

The last 11 rows of 5 small packages were removed. SecretManagerClient of doeff-google-secret-manager (group "Violation — move into a handler") is the type of the client argument of production_handlers, so the inventory reads it as a handler setting type and it moved to the group "Allowed — handler setting type" of the allowed table (ADR-DOE-API-001 R2). KeptReaders of doeff-events and AsyncTimeRuntime and SyncTimeRuntime of doeff-time (group "Violation — annotate the factory arguments or move inside") are parts the handlers build inside and are the type of no handler or factory argument, and MacroRecord of doeff-hy (group "Violation — move to an inner module") is read only by doeff's own tools, so the 4 names were removed from the entry points and are read from their inner modules (0 callers in outside repos). DEFAULT_FILE_PATTERNS and DoeffAdrHyFile of doeff-adr (group "Boundary — pytest plugin registration") are not read by pytest by name — the pytest11 entry point loads doeff_adr._pytest_plugin — so they were removed from the entry point after the callers in outside repos were rewritten (agora-controllers reads the patterns from doeff_adr._pytest_plugin; jev-proxy, which pins an older doeff commit, collects its Hy tests with the ini doeff_hy_test_files instead of DoeffAdrHyFile when it raises the pin); the 3 groups became empty and disappeared.

The group "Boundary — bus event type" became empty and disappeared. It held the event classes that a package's handler Publishes to the bus and that the body names and receives with WaitForEvent and WaitForEvents (the 7 names StopArrived, SourceFailed, SourceStalled, SourceResumed, SourceMissed, SourceStarted and TimerFired of doeff-events — 31 rows when split; after the forwarding modules were removed, 7 rows at the entry point remained). The answer of a wait is decided by the type the body names and cannot be written as one type in the T of EffectBase[T], so the waiting effect class now declares the package's bus events in its own __doeff_bus_events__, the inventory's answer_types reads them as the wait's answer types, and the 7 rows moved to the group "Allowed — effect answer type" of the allowed table. This group had been split off from the group "Violation — write the effect's answer type"; the 21 rows for the answers of Publish and PublishGap in that group (including NoticeSent and NoticeGapTold moved into it) write their answer types in the effect and moved to the allowed table, and the 4 rows of MarkGap (the value of when_unsent of NoticeRoute — no effect's answer) moved to the group "Boundary — handler setting type", the same as Drop and WhenUnsent of the same choice.

The 179 rows (20 packages, 109 names) of the group "Boundary — handler setting type" were moved because the allowed group "Allowed — handler setting type", whose shape the inventory verifies (a type defined by that package that appears in the annotations of handlers, handler classes and factory arguments exposed by the same package — following fields of setting types defined by the package; the inventory's settings), was added: the 112 rows that fit the shape (18 packages, 64 names) and 3 rows in "added names" moved to the allowed table with the basis ADR-DOE-API-001 R2, and the group disappeared. Of the 67 rows that do not fit (9 packages, 45 names — appearing in no exposed handler or factory argument), the 66 rows of types moved to the group "Violation — annotate the factory arguments or move inside", and the 1 row of the function default_session_backend to the group "Violation — move to an inner module". If it is a type passed to a handler, write the type in the argument of the factory or handler that takes it (a Hy defn argument, or an unannotated backend=None, etc.) and move it to the allowed table; if it is not passed, move it inside.

The 3 rows of choice, noul and score (functions that build a Question) of the doeff-system-one group "Violation — annotate the effect field or move inside" were removed. The 3 functions were removed after rewriting the callers in outside repos (rulebook/core.py of agent-commons; first_reader.hy and 2 tests of agora-controllers) and callers inside doeff to Question(kind=…, instructions=…, options=…/levels=…) (the order of R1 and R20). The group keeps the 3 rows of answer_choice, answer_noul and answer_score (functions that build an Answer), which were moved into it.

The last 2 rows of ChangedRow (event_source, memory) of the doeff-records group "Violation — annotate the effect field or move inside" were removed. The signal-type contract is written as the Protocol KeyedSignal (a read-only field keys: tuple[ChangedRow, ...] — a shape that a frozen dataclass field fits; placed in the inner _values and not public), and the annotation of the binding SignalTables.signal was changed from the bare type to type[KeyedSignal]. The inventory also reads the return type of a Protocol property as a field, so following handler argument bindings → SignalTables.signal → KeyedSignal.keys, ChangedRow appears in settings. The 2 rows moved to the group "Allowed — handler setting type" on the basis of R2.

The doeff-system-one group "Violation — annotate the effect field or move inside" became empty and disappeared. answer_choice, answer_noul and answer_score (functions that build an Answer) were removed: the confidence formula of noul (distance from 0.5 × 2 — which existed in three places, among them doeff-system-one and doeff-jev) was moved to a single place, the class method Answer.noul of Judge's answer type Answer, and the callers of choice and score were rewritten to Answer(kind=…, value=…, confidence=…). No repo that reads doeff's main has callers; the callers in the tests of agent-commons and dotfiles, which read a pinned doeff version, will be rewritten to Answer.noul and Answer(…) when the version is raised.

Of the 19 rows of the doeff-core-effects group "Violation — annotate the factory arguments or move inside", 15 left the table. The 9 rows of the 5 types handed to handlers moved to the group "Allowed — handler setting type" of the allowed table on the basis of R2: ClickHouseDatabase and PostgresDatabase already appear in handler arguments; PostgresTimeouts is now written in the annotation of the timeouts argument of PostgresConnections; InMemoryStorage and SQLiteStorage (the two storages the package ships) are now written in the annotation of the storage argument of memo_handler and cache_handler. The 6 names with 6 rows that no handler receives (WebEdge, MemoryLatestStore, ExitEnd — state a handler builds inside itself; StepBudget, SpentStepBudget, ProcessStepBudget — the state of the process step budget that arm_step_budget of the inner _scheduler keeps) were removed from the entry point and stay only in their inner modules (0 callers in outside repos; the tests read them from the inner modules). 4 rows stay, both argument types of a public program helper rather than of a handler: StackDumpLedger (3 rows — the argument and answer of stack_dumps_at; agora-controllers builds its own stack dump handler with the two, so the outside caller is rewritten first, the order of R20) and SqliteFile (1 row — the argument of open_sqlite_files, whose answer SqliteFiles is what the handler receives).

The last 43 rows of doeff-records were removed and its entry became empty. The submodules they name (admission, http_server, laws, main, maintenance, memory, pg, pg_sql, schema_digest, service, typed, values, wire) are all hidden with _ (R5), so the rows were read by name and root alone as the 13 names the entry point shows, and the inventory verifies an allowed shape for each: the 9 schema declaration types (ByKeySuffix, DescendingWithin, FieldDecl, KeepFor, KeepForever, RecordsSchema, RememberKeysFor, RememberNoKeys, TableDecl — reached from MemoryStore.schema and PreparedStore.schema through RecordsSchema.tables and the fields of TableDecl and StreamDecl) are handler setting types, RowChanged and RowRemoved are effect answer types (ChangeLog.changes, Changes.items), StoreUnreachable at the entry point is the exception class of the pg handler (the record of the same name in http_server is no longer shown), and purge_expired at the entry point is the program helper of pg (R25). 11 of the names already had rows in the allowed table; DescendingWithin and FieldDecl (the 2 rows of the group "Violation — annotate the factory arguments or move inside") moved to the group "Allowed — handler setting type" on the basis of R2.

The last 4 rows of the doeff-core-effects group "Violation — annotate the factory arguments or move inside" were removed and the doeff-core-effects entry became empty. StackDumpLedger and stack_dumps_at (the ledger and counting of the stack-dump watchdog) left the entry point and stay in the inner _stack_dump_effects: the factory watched_stack_dump_handler(watch) now holds the ledger, takes only the real watchdog as a function of the new deadline, and builds memory_stack_dump_handler and faulthandler_stack_dump_handler. SqliteFile left the entry point and stays in the inner _sqlite_file_sql: open_sqlite_files now takes a dict of database name to file path. The outside caller (agora-controllers controllers/foundation/stack_dumps.hy and sqlite_store.hy) was rewritten first, the order of ADR-DOE-API-001 R20 (doeff efc1c68d, agora-controllers 696d8c684d); the 3 rows of stack_dumps_at in the group "Allowed — program helper" of the allowed table were removed with them.

added_names.name: simulate_fold
added_names.reason: Simulation base: assembles the fold in the same shape as production, runs it with run using sim_time_handler for the clock and a memory EventBus for the bus, and returns the fold's answer. It is public so that users who measure a job with the caller's simulated handlers (the re-hosting of agora's jobs) need not copy the assembly. It runs a program and returns a value, so it fits none of the groups of effect, handler, or program helper. The assembly is pinned by packages/doeff-stream/tests/test_simulate_fold.py

added_names.name: WORKSPACE_SITE
added_names.reason: The production location and wait seconds passed to workspace-volumes-api, the production handler of the workspace volume (the Longhorn namespace, the ConfigMap of values, and the dir of requests to the mount helper — the same paths as the declaration of the node-h Pod). A job's child does not inherit the env WORKER_WORKSPACE_MOUNT_DIR, so the user (agora-controllers) receives the production values from the entry point. That they equal the declaration is pinned by tests/test_workspace_mount.py and tests/test_workspace_volumes.py

added_names.name: OUTBOX_RERAN
added_names.reason: Row kind (reran) of the notification-destination outbox added by re-running a detached task. As with OUTBOX_ENDED and OUTBOX_QUEUED_OVERDUE of the same module, it is a value passed to :kinds of AwaitDetachedOutbox, and users read it from the entry point (it is not listed in the fixed name list of the old path)

added_names.name: fold
added_names.reason: The runtime entry of doeff-stream. When a step returns a Program, fold itself wraps that Program with a handler (_refuse_every_effect) that refuses every effect — if callers had to wrap it, a step that forgot would be able to emit effects, so fold wraps it, on the condition set by the owners of cli_host and scheduling. It wraps only around the step's Program and touches neither run nor the caller's handlers. That it refuses is pinned by packages/doeff-stream/tests/test_program_step.py
